Subject: Redlined Order Form + questions on invoicing cadence

Hi Karthik —

Attached is CloudVista's redline of the Order Form (v3). We made a few changes on our side to the pricing schedule and the minimum-commit ladder. Key asks:

- Can Redwood confirm whether the activation fee can be invoiced upfront or amortized across Q1 invoices?
- We proposed Net45 on the Order Form; is Net30 a hard requirement for Redwood billing?
- Tax: we flagged VAT/responsibility language to reflect reverse-charge where applicable.

I attached a spreadsheet that shows our preferred invoice split by entity (tab: invoicing_flow). Please review and let me know who from Redwood legal/finance we should loop in for the redline discussion.

Attachments: CloudVista_OrderForm_Redline_v3.pdf (redline), pricing_schedule_v3.xlsx (invoice split)

Thanks — looking to close next week if possible.

Liz Carter
Head of Procurement
CloudVista Inc.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Liz Carter <liz.carter@cloudvista.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redlined Order Form + questions on invoicing cadence

Liz —

Thanks for the redlines and the spreadsheet — appreciate the clear tabbed breakdown. Looping in Kimberly (billing ops) and Marissa (commercials) to confirm the invoice routing and tax handling.

Quick thoughts before legal weighs in:
- Activation fee: we prefer invoicing activation upfront (one-time charge) but are willing to discuss amortization if CloudVista needs a phased cashflow. Need to confirm the amount that would be amortized and the impact on revenue recognition (cc Marissa).
- Net terms: our standard is Net30 for new enterprise commits; we can consider Net45 for qualified customers with an approved credit profile and an ARR commit — can procurement share the preferred payment cadence and whether a PO will be issued?
- VAT/reverse-charge: Kimberly, please validate whether Redwood can accept reverse-charge mechanics for CloudVista entities in the EU and what evidence we'd need.

Can Jonas (legal) take first pass on the redline? If possible, we should try to surface any MSA-level conflicts (jurisdiction, indemnity, data residency) so CloudVista knows what to expect.

Next steps: Jonas, would you accept the redline as-is for review and prepare a short summary of material commercial/legal asks we should escalate? Liz — we can schedule a 30-min call tomorrow or Monday to align on the invoice mapping.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Liz Carter <liz.carter@cloudvista.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redlined Order Form + questions on invoicing cadence

Karthik / Liz —

Reviewed the pricing_schedule_v3.xlsx (tab: invoicing_flow). A few operational notes from billing/finance:

- Invoicing entity: Redwood can invoice the Redwood US entity for CloudVista US entities and Redwood EU entity for EU-based CloudVista entities, but we need the official remit-to PO numbers and tax IDs for each invoicing entity.
- VAT: for reverse-charge, we require a valid VAT ID and an attestation that the recipient will self-account. Please provide the VAT ID list per entity in the spreadsheet; we can add a column for evidence type.
- Net terms: Net30 is preferred. If CloudVista requests Net45, we need a signed credit exception and a revised payment schedule in the Order Form.
- Activation fee amortization is possible but requires a short accounting memo and that CloudVista accepts a 12-month amortization schedule (if activation is material).

I'll attach a billing checklist we typically send (attachment stub: redwood_billing_requirements.pdf). If CloudVista can populate the missing PO/VAT values in the sheet we can re-run the invoice mapping and provide final invoice entity recommendations.

—Kimberly Park
Director, Billing Operations
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Michael Liu <michael.liu@cloudvista.com>, Liz Carter <liz.carter@cloudvista.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 15:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redlined Order Form + questions on invoicing cadence

Michael / Liz —

Thanks for the redline. I looked through CloudVista_OrderForm_Redline_v3.pdf and outlined the material legal/commercial items below — I tried to keep this high level to speed review: 

1) Minimum commit ladder (Section 2): CloudVista moved to a stepped commit that reduces early-period commitment. Redwood can accept a revised staircase but requests a firm 60-day notice for any downshift and a true-up clause at quarter close.

2) Activation fee (Section 4): Redwood's standard is a one-time activation invoice. If CloudVista needs amortization, our proposed alternative is amortize over 6 months (not 12) with the full invoiced amount remaining due on standard payment terms. This addresses revenue recognition and operational complexity.

3) Net terms (Section 7): We can consider Net45 as a commercial concession for customers with approved credit exceptions. To implement, add a short credit-exception appendix to the Order Form listing approved entities and the effective term.

4) Taxes and VAT (Section 9): We accept reverse-charge where legally applicable, provided CloudVista supplies VAT IDs and signed attestations. Otherwise Redwood will invoice VAT and CloudVista will seek recovery per local rules.

5) Governing law / jurisdiction (MSA §14): CloudVista's proposed change to a non-CA forum conflicts with our standard MSA. We're open to a compromise (mutual arbitration clause or CA courts for IP/data disputes).

Action items for CloudVista: please confirm which legal route you prefer on governing law and provide VAT IDs.

I've uploaded a clean redline with inline comments to the Drive link and generated a DocuSign envelope for the Order Form (link below). If CloudVista is comfortable with the 6-month amortization option and the credit-exception appendix, we can move to countersignature by end of week.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/EXAMPLE/CloudVista-Redline-2025
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-pricing

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercials
Redwood Inference
